findings.issue_text: [BUG] Removing the cacheMu serialization from BuildIndex breaks the build path for file-backed indices: concurrent builds for the same key can race on the same directory, causing build failures or index file corruption, since getOrCreateIndex still lazily creates indices after startup

[ADVISORY] NewResourceServer now calls s.Init(ctx) synchronously and fails construction on any error, converting previously per-request lazy failures into hard process startup failures that can crash-loop Grafana on transient DB errors or slow index builds

[BUG] s.search.TotalDocs() in the 'search index initialized' log executes before the async build goroutine has populated the indices, so total_docs logs 0 or a partial count on every startup, producing a misleading metric

[ADVISORY] Unconditionally skipping the module_server_test for postgres permanently removes the only integration coverage for the instrumentation-server-with-storage-target path on the primary production database, leaving regressions from this PR's startup-ordering changes undetected in CI

[ADVISORY] The postgres branch of the integration test is skipped with 'TODO - fix this test for postgres' and no replacement verification exists, so the PR's central behavioral change (eager Init in NewResourceServer, removal of lazy Init() guards from RPCs) ships with zero CI verification on postgres; a constructor-time init regression on postgres schemas passes CI green

[BUG] Init at constructor time only captures synchronous init errors in s.initErr; failures inside the background goroutine of search.init set s.initErr after the constructor has already returned, and since all per-RPC Init(ctx) guards were removed, nothing ever checks s.initErr — the server serves traffic with a broken search index and no watcher, silently

[ADVISORY] Reordering initWatcher() to run after s.search.init(ctx) drops the ordering guarantee that the watcher captures events concurrent with initial index building, so writes committed by other instances between the snapshot read and watcher start are never indexed — the index is permanently stale for those keys until the next write

[ADVISORY] Removing the whole-build b.cacheMu.Lock() in bleve.go and holding it only around b.cache[key] = idx allows concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key to both create a bleve index for the same on-disk directory, silently discarding the first index and its documents, with potential bolt file corruption/locking from double bleve.New on the same path

[ADVISORY] Every public RPC method lost its Init(ctx) guard with no test asserting that a server obtained from a path other than NewResourceServer is initialized, so any direct construction of the server struct yields a server whose watcher/search were never started and every RPC silently succeeds against an unindexed store

[ADVISORY] NewResourceServer now calls s.Init(ctx) synchronously in the constructor and returns an error, converting per-request lazy failure into a hard startup failure — a lifecycle/availability semantics change unrelated to the PR's stated performance intent; instances with failed or slow search index builds now fail to start entirely and rolling deploys can stall

[BUG] initWatcher() is reordered to run after s.search.init(ctx), so writes committed after the index snapshot but before watcher startup are never delivered and the freshly built index silently omits them, causing documents created during startup to vanish from search results

[ADVISORY] All eleven per-method s.Init(ctx) guards are deleted with no structural guarantee that every construction path calls Init, so any path building the struct directly serves requests against an uninitialized watcher/search with no error; also Init(ctx) runs on the constructor's context which can be cancelled mid-index-build with no retry path

[ADVISORY] The postgres integration test is permanently skipped with a TODO and no tracking issue, unrelated to the PR's performance scope — a coverage regression that leaves constructor-time init behavior on postgres untested in CI

[ADVISORY] The cacheMu lock guarding BuildIndex is narrowed to only the final cache write, removing mutual exclusion that prevented two concurrent builds for the same NamespacedResource key; nothing in the diff replaces that serialization, risking wasted duplicate builds and potential on-disk index corruption on the file-backed path

[BUG] Init reordering in server.Init: initWatcher() now runs after s.search.init(ctx), creating a window where resource writes between the index build snapshot and watcher start produce no WrittenEvent consumed by the search index, leaving documents permanently missing from the index and causing stale search results for resources modified during startup.

[BUG] BuildIndex lock scope reduction in bleve.go: removing the top-level cacheMu lock lets concurrent callers for the same NamespacedResource key both construct an index — for on-disk indexes the second fails bleve's file lock and errors out a valid in-flight build; for mem-only indexes the later cache write discards the first index, leaking memory and losing already-fed documents.

[BUG] NewResourceServer now calls s.Init(ctx) with the caller-supplied constructor context, so the watcher and search background work bind to one constructor-time context — a request-scoped or timeout-scoped context causes the watcher to die on cancellation while the server keeps serving CRUD, silently stopping search index updates.

[ADVISORY] Lazy per-request Init replaced by hard constructor-time Init turns a previously per-request failure into a hard startup failure of the whole resource server, making Grafana unbootable where the old design degraded search only.

[ADVISORY] The integration test exercising the full storage-server path is skipped for postgres in CI while this PR changes that server's startup/init sequencing and lock behavior, so postgres-specific init failures in the changed code ship to prod undetected.

[ADVISORY] Init is removed from every RPC handler but the method and s.initErr field remain public surface — out-of-tree embedders constructing the server directly without NewResourceServer now call Search/List/Watch against a never-initialized server with nil search or no watcher, with no lazy init recovery or guard asserting initialization at RPC entry.

[ADVISORY] Lazy per-request initialization in the resource server was moved into NewResourceServer as a hard constructor call and all per-RPC Init guards were deleted, so any init failure now becomes a fatal startup failure causing crash-looping pods instead of a degraded-but-running server, with no config flag to revert to lazy behavior

[ADVISORY] Init ordering was silently swapped so search index is built before the watcher starts, causing writes committed during index building to be missed by the watcher and the index to be immediately stale until a full reindex

[ADVISORY] Removing the cacheMu lock around BuildIndex allows two concurrent callers building the same NamespacedResource key to both run the full builder and create file-backed bleve indexes at the same directory, leaving a stale on-disk index from the loser and breaking the 'at most one live index per key' invariant

[ADVISORY] The postgres integration test is skipped with a t.Skip and TODO comment instead of fixing the incompatibility, so the primary integration path for the unified storage server loses all postgres CI coverage indefinitely and known postgres defects are shipped anyway

[ADVISORY] Moving s.Init(ctx) out of request handlers into NewResourceServer converts per-request retryable init failures into hard process-startup failures — transient infrastructure errors (e.g., search backend unavailable, disk error creating bleve index dirs) now prevent the whole Grafana process from booting, with no retry path, instead of a degraded-but-alive server

[ADVISORY] pkg/server/module_server_test.go:35-38 — permanent t.Skip for postgres removes the only test coverage of the newly-changed NewResourceServer eager-init construction semantics (constructor-time init failure returning nil, err), so regressions in eager init for postgres pass CI with a green suite while Drone postgres builds are broken; a unit-level test of NewResourceServer/Init ordering should have been added instead of skipping.

[ADVISORY] pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:300-310 — Init order swapped so search index is built before the watcher starts, creating an untested window where events written after search.init snapshots the index but before initWatcher registers are silently absent from the index, causing user-visible missing search results until the next full rebuild; no test exercises this window or asserts eventual indexing of writes landing in it.

[ADVISORY] pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:85-140 — narrowing the cache-mutex scope from 'whole build' to 'map write only' allows two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key to each build a full index, with the loser's documents-built counter and b.cache[key] overwrite silently discarded; concurrent BuildIndex for the same key is untested, leaving last-writer-wins semantics unverified.

[ADVISORY] Lazy per-request Init is replaced with eager init in NewResourceServer, making initialization failure (e.g., search index build error) a hard constructor failure, converting a degraded-service condition into a full process boot failure on the same underlying fault

[ADVISORY] Ordering change: search.init (full index build, potentially minutes on large tenants) now runs before initWatcher, so events written to the DB between index-build start and watcher start are never seen by the index, causing newly created/updated resources during the build window to be missing from search results until the next full reindex

[ADVISORY] NewResourceServer now calls s.Init(ctx) synchronously, converting previously-lazy per-request initialization failures (search index build, watcher setup, backend access) into hard startup failures — transient DB errors or corrupt bleve directories now prevent the entire storage server from starting instead of serving degraded reads/writes with retry

[ADVISORY] Init ordering inverted: s.search.init(ctx) (full index build) completes before s.initWatcher() starts, so resources written during index building are permanently missing from the search index — silent stale search results with no error

[ADVISORY] All request-time Init guards were deleted from Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/History/Origin/IsHealthy/PutBlob/GetBlob with nothing replacing them on the request path, so servers constructed outside NewResourceServer (test harnesses, mocks, callers ignoring constructor error) hit nil-pointer panics instead of clean init errors

[ADVISORY] cacheMu.Lock() guarding the entire BuildIndex body was narrowed to only the final cache write, allowing two concurrent getOrCreateIndex callers for the same key to run full index builds in parallel — doubled DB full-scans and concurrent writes to the same on-disk bleve directory

[ADVISORY] search.go init() logs 'search index initialized' and emits metrics immediately after spawning the async build goroutine, so the log reports fabricated total_docs of 0-or-stale and near-zero duration before the build completes, misleading operators debugging slow index builds

[ADVISORY] Postgres integration test in module_server_test.go is skipped with a TODO rather than fixed, leaving zero instrumentation-server integration coverage on all CI database backends, leaving this diff's biggest behavioral change unverified against the primary production database

goldens.comment: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.

Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes initialization from per-request lazy `s.Init(ctx)` calls (removed from Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/etc.) to eager initialization in `NewResourceServer` via `err := s.Init(ctx)` and returning the error. This makes construction fail if `Init` (which now includes `s.search.init(ctx)` and `s.initWatcher()`) errors, shifting failures to startup. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] s.search.TotalDocs() in the 'search index initialized' log executes before the async build goroutine has populated the indices, so total_docs logs 0 or a partial count on every startup, producing a misleading metric

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go, searchSupport.init() appears to kick off work in an async goroutine (the `go func() { ... }()` around the added log location), and then immediately computes `end := time.Now().Unix()` and logs `s.search.TotalDocs()`. From what’s shown, there is no synchronization/wait before the log, so `total_docs` can reflect an empty/partial index at that moment, making the log misleading. This affects observability rather than correctness of indexing behavior (based on the diff alone).

While the claim that it is the *only* coverage for that path cannot be verified from this diff alone, the change clearly reduces Postgres integration coverage right when the PR also changes server initialization/startup ordering in `pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go` (moving `Init` into `NewResourceServer` and removing per-RPC `Init` calls).

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a `t.Skip` for `dbType == "postgres"` in `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer` with a TODO comment, so that integration path won’t run under postgres. In the same PR, `NewResourceServer` now eagerly calls `s.Init(ctx)` and the per-RPC `Init(ctx)` guards are removed, which is a nontrivial behavioral change that could be backend-sensitive. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Init at constructor time only captures synchronous init errors in s.initErr; failures inside the background goroutine of search.init set s.initErr after the constructor has already returned, and since all per-RPC Init(ctx) guards were removed, nothing ever checks s.initErr — the server serves traffic with a broken search index and no watcher, silently

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns an error if `Init` sets `s.initErr` (it even logs and returns `nil, err`). So `s.initErr` *is* checked at construction time. The finding’s core claim that “nothing ever checks s.initErr” after removing per-RPC `Init(ctx)` guards is not supported by the diff. Also, the diff does not show any code where a background goroutine inside `search.init` later assigns to `s.initErr`, so the asserted silent-failure path cannot be verified from what’s shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Reordering initWatcher() to run after s.search.init(ctx) drops the ordering guarantee that the watcher captures events concurrent with initial index building, so writes committed by other instances between the snapshot read and watcher start are never indexed — the index is permanently stale for those keys until the next write

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go, Init() now calls s.search.init(ctx) before s.initWatcher() (previously watcher started first). If the watcher is the mechanism that streams WrittenEvent updates into the search index, then building the initial index without the watcher running can miss writes that occur during index initialization, leaving the index behind until subsequent writes re-touch those keys. The diff shows an explicit ordering change that plausibly creates this correctness gap.

[ADVISORY] Every public RPC method lost its Init(ctx) guard with no test asserting that a server obtained from a path other than NewResourceServer is initialized, so any direct construction of the server struct yields a server whose watcher/search were never started and every RPC silently succeeds against an unindexed store

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes `s.Init(ctx)` calls from all RPC handlers (e.g., `Create`, `Update`, `Read`, `Watch`, `Search`, etc. in `pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go`) and moves initialization to `NewResourceServer()` which now calls `s.Init(ctx)` before returning. This makes correctness depend on all callers obtaining servers exclusively via `NewResourceServer`; any in-package direct construction of the unexported `server` (or another constructor not shown here) would bypass init, so watcher/search index setup in `Init()` would never run. The finding’s broader claim about tests and ‘silently succeeds’ behavior isn’t directly verifiable from the diff, but the loss of per-RPC init guards and reliance on the constructor is a concrete, review-relevant concern introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] NewResourceServer now calls s.Init(ctx) synchronously in the constructor and returns an error, converting per-request lazy failure into a hard startup failure — a lifecycle/availability semantics change unrelated to the PR's stated performance intent; instances with failed or slow search index builds now fail to start entirely and rolling deploys can stall

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a clear lifecycle semantics change: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` synchronously and returns an error on failure (server.go `NewResourceServer`: added `err := s.Init(ctx)` block). At the same time, the prior per-request lazy initialization (`if err := s.Init(ctx); err != nil { ... }`) was removed from multiple RPC handlers (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/History/Origin/IsHealthy/PutBlob/GetBlob). Since `Init` runs `s.search.init(ctx)` (which can build/initialize the search index) and `s.initWatcher()`, any failure or slowness there now affects constructor/startup rather than individual requests, which can impact availability/rollout behavior. PR intent ('performance') isn’t verifiable from the diff, but the operational behavior change is real and review-worthy.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] initWatcher() is reordered to run after s.search.init(ctx), so writes committed after the index snapshot but before watcher startup are never delivered and the freshly built index silently omits them, causing documents created during startup to vanish from search results

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go Init(), the diff explicitly moves `s.initWatcher()` to run *after* `s.search.init(ctx)` (previously watcher started before index init). If the watcher is responsible for delivering post-snapshot write events to the search index, this reordering creates a clear window where writes can be committed after the index is built/snapshotted but before the watcher starts, meaning those events would not be observed/indexed and search could miss documents created during startup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] All eleven per-method s.Init(ctx) guards are deleted with no structural guarantee that every construction path calls Init, so any path building the struct directly serves requests against an uninitialized watcher/search with no error; also Init(ctx) runs on the constructor's context which can be cancelled mid-index-build with no retry path

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the repeated per-RPC `s.Init(ctx)` calls (e.g., `Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/...`) and instead adds a single `s.Init(ctx)` call in `NewResourceServer` before returning the server. That does create a potential correctness risk *if* any code can construct `server` without going through `NewResourceServer`, because then requests would run without initialization and there are no longer per-method guards. However, the diff does not show whether such alternate construction paths exist, so the claim of “no structural guarantee” is not fully verifiable from the diff alone. Likewise, the concern about Init using a cancelable constructor context is not verifiable because the origin/lifetime of `ctx` in `NewResourceServer` is not shown in the provided diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The postgres integration test is permanently skipped with a TODO and no tracking issue, unrelated to the PR's performance scope — a coverage regression that leaves constructor-time init behavior on postgres untested in CI

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a new unconditional skip for `dbType == "postgres"` in `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer` with a `// TODO - fix this test for postgres` comment and no reference to a tracking issue (module_server_test.go). That is a concrete, diff-grounded reduction in CI coverage for postgres runs. Separately, the PR changes init behavior to constructor-time `NewResourceServer` calling `s.Init(ctx)` and removes per-RPC `Init` calls (server.go), so skipping postgres integration tests can leave postgres-specific init paths less exercised in CI.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The cacheMu lock guarding BuildIndex is narrowed to only the final cache write, removing mutual exclusion that prevented two concurrent builds for the same NamespacedResource key; nothing in the diff replaces that serialization, risking wasted duplicate builds and potential on-disk index corruption on the file-backed path

[BUG] Init reordering in server.Init: initWatcher() now runs after s.search.init(ctx), creating a window where resource writes between the index build snapshot and watcher start produce no WrittenEvent consumed by the search index, leaving documents permanently missing from the index and causing stale search results for resources modified during startup.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does reorder initialization in `server.Init`: it now calls `s.search.init(ctx)` before `s.initWatcher()` (previously watcher started first). That ordering change could plausibly create a missed-update window if `search.init` builds an index snapshot and relies on the watcher to deliver subsequent `WrittenEvent`s. However, from the diff alone we cannot verify the watcher’s semantics (e.g., whether it starts from a known resource version, replays, or whether the server can receive concurrent writes during `NewResourceServer` now that it calls `s.Init(ctx)` before returning). So the risk is real and diff-grounded, but the “permanently missing documents” behavior isn’t conclusively provable from this patch alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] BuildIndex lock scope reduction in bleve.go: removing the top-level cacheMu lock lets concurrent callers for the same NamespacedResource key both construct an index — for on-disk indexes the second fails bleve's file lock and errors out a valid in-flight build; for mem-only indexes the later cache write discards the first index, leaking memory and losing already-fed documents.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, BuildIndex previously held b.cacheMu for the entire method (including index creation), but the diff removes that and now only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx`. This means concurrent callers for the same `key` can both proceed to create an index (including `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` for on-disk indexes) before either writes to the cache, so the cache no longer serializes per-key builds. That can plausibly lead to two builders racing on the same directory and one failing, and/or one built index being overwritten in the cache by the other, as the finding describes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] NewResourceServer now calls s.Init(ctx) with the caller-supplied constructor context, so the watcher and search background work bind to one constructor-time context — a request-scoped or timeout-scoped context causes the watcher to die on cancellation while the server keeps serving CRUD, silently stopping search index updates.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)`, but it does not show where `ctx` comes from (the function signature doesn’t accept a caller-provided context), so the claim that this is a request-/timeout-scoped context is not verifiable from the diff. Also, `initWatcher()` does not take a context at all in the shown code, so the finding’s statement that the watcher binds to that constructor-time context is contradicted by the diff. While `s.search.init(ctx)` does receive a context, the diff snippet alone doesn’t demonstrate that search background work will be canceled when that context is canceled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Lazy per-request Init replaced by hard constructor-time Init turns a previously per-request failure into a hard startup failure of the whole resource server, making Grafana unbootable where the old design degraded search only.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly moves initialization from per-request calls (removed `if err := s.Init(ctx); err != nil { ... }` in Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/History/Origin/IsHealthy/PutBlob/GetBlob) to constructor time: `NewResourceServer` now calls `err := s.Init(ctx)` and returns `nil, err` on failure. That does turn an init failure from a request-time error into a server-construction/startup failure. However, the finding’s claim that the old design “degraded search only” isn’t supported by the diff: previously any handler that called `Init` would fail if `Init` returned an error, not just search. Still, the startup-failure behavior change is real and potentially impactful.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The integration test exercising the full storage-server path is skipped for postgres in CI while this PR changes that server's startup/init sequencing and lock behavior, so postgres-specific init failures in the changed code ship to prod undetected.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a postgres skip in an integration test (`pkg/server/module_server_test.go`: `if dbType == "postgres" { t.Skip(...) }`), reducing CI coverage for postgres. In the same PR, nontrivial behavior changes are made to the storage/resource server init sequencing (e.g., `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and request handlers no longer call `Init`) and lock behavior in the bleve backend (`BuildIndex` no longer holds `cacheMu` across the build, only around `b.cache[key]=idx`). With postgres CI coverage for at least this integration path now disabled, postgres-specific init/ordering issues in the changed code could go undetected. This is a concrete test/coverage risk grounded in the diff, not a proven defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Init is removed from every RPC handler but the method and s.initErr field remain public surface — out-of-tree embedders constructing the server directly without NewResourceServer now call Search/List/Watch against a never-initialized server with nil search or no watcher, with no lazy init recovery or guard asserting initialization at RPC entry.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the per-RPC `s.Init(ctx)` calls from `Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/...` and instead calls `s.Init(ctx)` only in `NewResourceServer` (and returns an error if init fails). This changes the contract from lazy init-at-RPC-entry to eager init-at-construction. If any code path constructs/obtains a `*server` without going through `NewResourceServer`, the RPC methods no longer self-heal by initializing and could run with unstarted watcher or nil/unfinished search. However, the diff does not show whether out-of-tree consumers can actually construct `*server` directly (the concrete type is unexported in the shown method receivers), so the “out-of-tree embedders” claim isn’t fully verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Lazy per-request initialization in the resource server was moved into NewResourceServer as a hard constructor call and all per-RPC Init guards were deleted, so any init failure now becomes a fatal startup failure causing crash-looping pods instead of a degraded-but-running server, with no config flag to revert to lazy behavior

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns an error on failure (`return nil, err`), and all per-RPC `if err := s.Init(ctx); err != nil { ... }` guards were removed from methods like `Create`, `Update`, `Read`, `Watch`, `Search`, etc. This is a real, diff-grounded behavioral change: initialization errors are now surfaced at construction time rather than lazily on first request. Whether that results in “crash-looping pods” depends on external wiring not shown, so it’s not verifiable as a concrete defect from the diff alone, but it is a significant operational/architecture concern introduced by the change, and no revert/config toggle is present in the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Init ordering was silently swapped so search index is built before the watcher starts, causing writes committed during index building to be missed by the watcher and the index to be immediately stale until a full reindex

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly swaps init order in server.Init: it now calls `s.search.init(ctx)` before `s.initWatcher()` (previously watcher started first). That makes the reviewer’s concern plausible: any writes/events occurring while the search index is being built won’t be observed until the watcher starts, potentially leaving the index stale unless the watcher replays from a known resource version. However, the diff does not show watcher semantics (e.g., whether it backfills/replays), so the claim of definite missed writes can’t be fully verified from this PR alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Removing the cacheMu lock around BuildIndex allows two concurrent callers building the same NamespacedResource key to both run the full builder and create file-backed bleve indexes at the same directory, leaving a stale on-disk index from the loser and breaking the 'at most one live index per key' invariant

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, BuildIndex previously held b.cacheMu for the entire function and now only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx`. With the lock removed from the build path, two concurrent callers for the same `key` can both proceed to `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` using the same deterministic `dir := filepath.Join(b.opts.Root, key.Namespace, fmt.Sprintf("%s.%s", ...))` and run the full builder concurrently. The diff shows no other synchronization or cache check in BuildIndex to prevent duplicate builds, so this can violate the intended single-live-index-per-key behavior and can race on the same on-disk directory.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The postgres integration test is skipped with a t.Skip and TODO comment instead of fixing the incompatibility, so the primary integration path for the unified storage server loses all postgres CI coverage indefinitely and known postgres defects are shipped anyway

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a postgres-specific `t.Skip` guarded by `if dbType == "postgres"` with a TODO comment in `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer` (pkg/server/module_server_test.go), meaning postgres will no longer run this integration test in CI. This is a concrete, diff-grounded reduction in postgres coverage rather than a direct runtime defect in production code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Moving s.Init(ctx) out of request handlers into NewResourceServer converts per-request retryable init failures into hard process-startup failures — transient infrastructure errors (e.g., search backend unavailable, disk error creating bleve index dirs) now prevent the whole Grafana process from booting, with no retry path, instead of a degraded-but-alive server

adjudication.rationale: The diff does move initialization from request-time to construction-time: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns an error if init fails (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go), and all request handlers (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/etc.) remove their `s.Init(ctx)` calls. This can make init failures surface during server creation rather than on first request, potentially turning a previously “server starts but endpoints fail” situation into a “resource server cannot be constructed” situation. However, the finding’s claim about a per-request retry path is not supported by the diff: `Init` uses `sync.Once` and stores `s.initErr`, so repeated per-request calls would not retry after an initial failure anyway—only defer when the failure is encountered.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] pkg/server/module_server_test.go:35-38 — permanent t.Skip for postgres removes the only test coverage of the newly-changed NewResourceServer eager-init construction semantics (constructor-time init failure returning nil, err), so regressions in eager init for postgres pass CI with a green suite while Drone postgres builds are broken; a unit-level test of NewResourceServer/Init ordering should have been added instead of skipping.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds an unconditional `t.Skip` for `dbType == "postgres"` in `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer` (pkg/server/module_server_test.go), which removes CI coverage for that integration test on postgres and can allow postgres-specific regressions to slip through green CI. However, the finding’s claim that this was the *only* test covering the newly changed `NewResourceServer` eager-init semantics cannot be verified from the diff alone (the test shown is in module_server_test.go and its linkage to `NewResourceServer` isn’t shown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:300-310 — Init order swapped so search index is built before the watcher starts, creating an untested window where events written after search.init snapshots the index but before initWatcher registers are silently absent from the index, causing user-visible missing search results until the next full rebuild; no test exercises this window or asserts eventual indexing of writes landing in it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does swap the Init() sequence in pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go so that s.search.init(ctx) runs before s.initWatcher() (the watcher-start block was moved below search init). That creates a plausible race window during initialization where writes/events occurring concurrently with Init could be missed by the watcher and thus not reflected in the index, and the diff shows no accompanying test for this scenario. However, the diff also moves Init() to run inside NewResourceServer() before returning the server, which may mean no RPC writes can occur in that window in typical startup, so the finding’s claim of a definite user-visible defect isn’t fully verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:85-140 — narrowing the cache-mutex scope from 'whole build' to 'map write only' allows two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key to each build a full index, with the loser's documents-built counter and b.cache[key] overwrite silently discarded; concurrent BuildIndex for the same key is untested, leaving last-writer-wins semantics unverified.
matched_golden_ids: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same race: the cache mutex no longer covers the entire BuildIndex execution, so concurrent calls for the same key can both perform the expensive index build and then race on the final cache write (last-writer-wins), discarding work/counters. This matches the golden comment’s root cause and effect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Lazy per-request Init is replaced with eager init in NewResourceServer, making initialization failure (e.g., search index build error) a hard constructor failure, converting a degraded-service condition into a full process boot failure on the same underlying fault

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an eager `s.Init(ctx)` call inside `NewResourceServer` and returns the error (`return nil, err`) on failure, while removing the per-request `Init` calls from RPC methods like `Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search` etc. This is a real behavior/architecture change: initialization failures that previously would surface when the first request hit (and could allow the process to stay up but have failing endpoints) now prevent the server from being constructed at all. However, the diff also contains comments indicating init is intended to block startup (e.g., `searchSupport.init` comment: "any failure will block startup"), so it’s not clearly a defect—more a deliberate change with operational implications.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Ordering change: search.init (full index build, potentially minutes on large tenants) now runs before initWatcher, so events written to the DB between index-build start and watcher start are never seen by the index, causing newly created/updated resources during the build window to be missing from search results until the next full reindex

adjudication.rationale: The diff in pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go changes Init() ordering: it now calls s.search.init(ctx) (full index build) before s.initWatcher() (previously watcher started first). This creates a real, diff-grounded risk window where writes occurring during a long index build might not be picked up by the watcher, depending on how initWatcher seeds its starting position/rv (not shown in the diff). The finding’s specific “never seen” outcome isn’t fully verifiable from the provided changes, but the ordering change and associated potential for missed updates is real and review-worthy.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] NewResourceServer now calls s.Init(ctx) synchronously, converting previously-lazy per-request initialization failures (search index build, watcher setup, backend access) into hard startup failures — transient DB errors or corrupt bleve directories now prevent the entire storage server from starting instead of serving degraded reads/writes with retry

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes initialization from lazy/per-request to eager/startup: `NewResourceServer` now calls `err := s.Init(ctx)` and returns error on failure, while per-RPC `s.Init(ctx)` calls were removed from `Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/...` in `server.go`. Since `Init()` performs search index initialization (`s.search.init(ctx)`) and watcher setup (`s.initWatcher()`), any error there now prevents `NewResourceServer` from returning a server at all, whereas previously the process could start and only fail requests until a later retry succeeds. Whether this is desired “fail fast” behavior or too strict is an architectural/product concern rather than a provable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Init ordering inverted: s.search.init(ctx) (full index build) completes before s.initWatcher() starts, so resources written during index building are permanently missing from the search index — silent stale search results with no error

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes Init() ordering: it now calls `s.search.init(ctx)` before `s.initWatcher()` (see `pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go`). This creates a plausible consistency/race risk where changes occurring during a full index build might not be observed by the watcher. However, the finding’s stronger claim (“permanently missing”, “silent stale results”) cannot be verified from the diff alone because `initWatcher()`/watch semantics and whether it replays from a resource version or catches up are not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] All request-time Init guards were deleted from Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/History/Origin/IsHealthy/PutBlob/GetBlob with nothing replacing them on the request path, so servers constructed outside NewResourceServer (test harnesses, mocks, callers ignoring constructor error) hit nil-pointer panics instead of clean init errors

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove per-request `s.Init(ctx)` calls from many RPC methods (e.g., `Create/Update/Delete/...`), and replaces that by calling `s.Init(ctx)` once inside `NewResourceServer` before returning (`pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go` adds `err := s.Init(ctx)` in the constructor). This changes the safety/contract: only servers built via `NewResourceServer` are guaranteed initialized; any code that constructs a `server` without that constructor (tests/mocks/manual instantiation) would no longer get request-path initialization. The finding’s specific claim about “nil-pointer panics” isn’t directly provable from the diff alone, but the removal of guards with init now centralized in the constructor is real and could break non-constructor usages.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] cacheMu.Lock() guarding the entire BuildIndex body was narrowed to only the final cache write, allowing two concurrent getOrCreateIndex callers for the same key to run full index builds in parallel — doubled DB full-scans and concurrent writes to the same on-disk bleve directory

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, BuildIndex previously held b.cacheMu.Lock()/Unlock() across the entire function body, but the diff removes that and now only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx`. This change makes it possible for two goroutines to concurrently execute the expensive index creation/build path for the same `key` (including `bleve.New(dir, ...)` for the same on-disk directory when `size > FileThreshold`) before either writes to the cache, which can lead to duplicate full builds and potential concurrent access to the same index directory.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] search.go init() logs 'search index initialized' and emits metrics immediately after spawning the async build goroutine, so the log reports fabricated total_docs of 0-or-stale and near-zero duration before the build completes, misleading operators debugging slow index builds

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go, init() now logs `s.log.Info("search index initialized", "duration_secs", end-start, "total_docs", s.search.TotalDocs())` immediately after launching an async goroutine that performs the index build (the `go func() { ... }()` started earlier in init). Since `end` is computed and the log/metrics are emitted without waiting for that goroutine to finish, `duration_secs` reflects only setup time (not build time) and `TotalDocs()` can be 0/stale until the build completes, which can mislead operators, but does not break functional behavior.
